Subject: Onramp sequencing — MSA/DPA/order form dependencies

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move from evaluation to a pilot. Procurement asked me to share a quick checklist and to confirm sequencing for the MSA, DPA, and order form so we can lock the pilot start date. Attached is a short procurement checklist that surfaced during our internal kickoff.

High-level asks from Biovista:
- Can we get a MAP showing who owns each legal/procurement step and expected turnaround windows?
- Are there any non-standard clauses in your standard MSA we should expect to discuss?
- What’s the expected timeline if we run legal and DPA review in parallel?

We’re targeting a contract signature window in early May so we can start pilot provisioning mid-May. Let me know any missing info and we can schedule a quick alignment call.

Attachments: Biovista_onramp_checklist.pdf

Regards,
Samantha Lee
VP, IT Procurement
Biovista Therapeutics

Date: 2027-04-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onramp sequencing — MSA/DPA/order form dependencies

Hi Samantha — thanks for the checklist. I’ve sketched a pragmatic MAP (attached) that sequences parallel reviews and highlights gating checkpoints so Biovista can hit an early May signature target. Key points up front:

- Legal (MSA redlines) and Security/DPA review can run in parallel; typical turnaround from our side for an initial redline set is 5–7 business days.
- Procurement sign-off (order form commercial terms) usually waits until core legal points are reconciled; we can preliminarily lock pricing and term length in the order form while legal closes concurrently.
- We require confirmation on data residency and KMS bring-your-own-key options for pilot; that will affect DPA language and onboarding lead times.

I attached Biovista_MAP_v1.xlsx — it includes: owners, proposed dates, acceptance gates, and the minimal artifacts we’ll need at each gate (e.g., evidence for SOC2, sample SLA appendix). Proposed timeline in the doc assumes we start legal review 2027-04-20 and target order-form signature 2027-05-03.

Can Karthik and Jonas review the MAP for legal/technical thumbs-up? Also, Samantha — can you confirm whether Biovista will require an HSM/KMS key in pilot? That will change a couple of acceptance requirements.

Thanks — I’ll block 30 minutes next week for a MAP walk-through if that helps.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Aisha / Samantha — quick legal read and proposed sequencing below. I’ve attached a redline of our MSA (RDW_MSA_v3_redline.docx) with the handful of commercial/legal items Biovista will likely flag.

Quick notes from legal:
- MSA: Exceptions we expect to discuss — indemnity reciprocity, liability cap carve-outs for data breaches, and intellectual property carve-outs related to model improvements. We can turn initial redlines in ~5 business days (by 2027-04-27) if there are no unusual provisions from Biovista.
- DPA: Provide SSO, data residency, KMS/BYOK options. DPA can be finalized in parallel; security should provide evidence pack (SOC2 report, subprocessors list) by 2027-04-26 to avoid delays.
- Order form: Commercial approval (pricing, seat counts, pilot term) can be agreed and placed on the signature-ready order form while legal and DPA finish wordsmithing.

Proposed consolidated timeline (from Redwood legal/ops perspective):
- 2027-04-20: Biovista confirms KMS/residency and returns the procurement checklist + target commercial terms.
- 2027-04-22: Redwood sends MSA redline (initial) and DPA draft to Biovista.
- 2027-04-26: Biovista returns legal comments (target).
- 2027-04-29: Redwood responds to redlines and aims to get to a near-final MSA.
- 2027-05-03: Order form signed and DocuSign envelope issued for MSA/DPA simultaneously (if both near-final).

I’ve attached RDW_MSA_v3_redline.docx (high-level redline + comments). Samantha — we’ll need the Biovista legal contact on the thread (name & email) to route document redlines directly. Also please provide the procurement PO number format if your finance team requires it on the order form.

DocuSign preview link: https://docusign.com/rdw/DocuSignLink?env=prod&id=9f2a

Subject: MAP finalization & next steps — target signature 2027-05-03

Samantha / Raj / Procurement Team — thanks for the quick turn. Summary and agreed next steps below; I’ve attached Biovista_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP with updated owners, due dates, and acceptance criteria).

Agreed sequencing and ownership (from MAP_v2):
- 2027-04-20 to 2027-04-26: Biovista provides KMS decision, procurement checklist items, and Biovista legal contact (owner: Samantha).
- 2027-04-22 to 2027-04-29: Redwood legal (Karthik) and Biovista legal exchange redlines (owner: Karthik / Biovista legal).
- 2027-04-22 to 2027-04-27: Security evidence pack exchange (SOC2, subprocessors) — owner: Neha (Redwood) / Biovista InfoSec.
- 2027-04-30 to 2027-05-02: Order form commercial sign-off and finance checks (owner: Marissa / Biovista procurement).
- 2027-05-03: Execute order form and issue DocuSign envelope for MSA/DPA simultaneously (target signature date).

Acceptance criteria for pilot provisioning (listed in MAP_v2):
- Signed order form and countersigned MSA or DocuSign envelope issued for both MSA & DPA.
- Security pack received and verified by Neha.
- Pilot environment provisioning window scheduled (tentative start 2027-05-10).

Open items for Biovista to confirm:
1) KMS BYOK required? (affects DPA and onboarding lead time)
2) Finance PO number format and whether PO is required to start provisioning pre-signature
3) Biovista legal primary contact (email + preferred turnaround)

Next steps:
- Samantha to confirm open items by COB 2027-04-27.
- Karthik to circulate updated redline based on Biovista legal comments by 2027-04-29.
- I’ll schedule a 30-minute MAP walk-through for 2027-04-28 at 10:00 AM PT — invite to follow.

Thanks all — closing this loop so we have a single source of truth. Attachments: Biovista_MAP_v2.xlsx.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
